claim: Antibody production depends on B cell internalization and presentation of antigens to helper T cells.
source: Antibody production depends on B cell internalization and presentation of antigens to helper T cells.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in immunology supported by scientific consensus.

claim: B cells form immune synapses to acquire antigens displayed by antigen-presenting cells.
source: To acquire antigens displayed by antigen-presenting cells, B cells form immune synapses and extract antigens by the mechanical activity of the acto-myosin cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of B cell biology.

claim: B cells extract antigens by the mechanical activity of the acto-myosin cytoskeleton.
source: To acquire antigens displayed by antigen-presenting cells, B cells form immune synapses and extract antigens by the mechanical activity of the acto-myosin cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is supported by previous research in the field.

claim: After initial cell spreading, F-actin in synapses of primary mouse B cells forms a highly dynamic pattern composed of actin foci interspersed with linear filaments and myosin IIa.
source: Here we show that after initial cell spreading, F-actin in synapses of primary mouse B cells and human B cell lines forms a highly dynamic pattern composed of actin foci interspersed with linear filaments and myosin IIa.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations presented in the manuscript, including microscopy data.

claim: After initial cell spreading, F-actin in synapses of human B cell lines forms a highly dynamic pattern composed of actin foci interspersed with linear filaments and myosin IIa.
source: Here we show that after initial cell spreading, F-actin in synapses of primary mouse B cells and human B cell lines forms a highly dynamic pattern composed of actin foci interspersed with linear filaments and myosin IIa.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The actin foci are generated by Arp2/3-mediated branched-actin polymerization.
source: The foci are generated by Arp2/3-mediated branched-actin polymerization and stochastically associate with antigen clusters to mediate internalization.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data including inhibitor studies and CRISPR targeting.

claim: Actin foci stochastically associate with antigen clusters to mediate internalization.
source: The foci are generated by Arp2/3-mediated branched-actin polymerization and stochastically associate with antigen clusters to mediate internalization.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy observations showing colocalization of foci with antigen clusters.

claim: Antigen extraction requires the activity of formins.
source: However, antigen extraction also requires the activity of formins, which reside near the foci and produce the interspersed filaments.
evidence: This is supported by inhibitor studies showing reduced antigen extraction upon formin inhibition.

claim: Formins reside near the actin foci.
source: However, antigen extraction also requires the activity of formins, which reside near the foci and produce the interspersed filaments.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data showing DIAPH1 localization near actin foci.

claim: Formins produce the interspersed filaments.
source: However, antigen extraction also requires the activity of formins, which reside near the foci and produce the interspersed filaments.
evidence: This is supported by inhibitor studies showing dispersal of fibers upon formin inhibition.

claim: A cooperation of branched-actin foci supported by linear filaments underlies B cell mechanics during antigen extraction.
source: Thus, a cooperation of branched-actin foci supported by linear filaments underlies B cell mechanics during antigen extraction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing both Arp2/3 and formins are required for antigen extraction.

claim: After antigen binding, the BCR undergoes endocytosis and delivers the antigen into intracellular processing compartments.
source: After antigen binding, the BCR undergoes endocytosis and delivers the antigen into intracellular processing compartments, where antigenic peptides are loaded onto major histocompatibility II (MHC II) proteins (Hoogeboom and Tolar, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Antigenic peptides are loaded onto major histocompatibility II (MHC II) proteins in intracellular processing compartments.
source: After antigen binding, the BCR undergoes endocytosis and delivers the antigen into intracellular processing compartments, where antigenic peptides are loaded onto major histocompatibility II (MHC II) proteins (Hoogeboom and Tolar, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Presentation of the peptide-MHC II complexes on the surfaces of B cells solicits T cell help.
source: Presentation of the peptide-MHC II complexes on the surfaces of B cells solicits T cell help and promotes B cell proliferation and differentiation into germinal center, memory and plasma cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: Presentation of the peptide-MHC II complexes on the surfaces of B cells promotes B cell proliferation and differentiation into germinal center, memory and plasma cells.
source: Presentation of the peptide-MHC II complexes on the surfaces of B cells solicits T cell help and promotes B cell proliferation and differentiation into germinal center, memory and plasma cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology.

claim: The uptake of soluble antigen by the BCR occurs predominantly via clathrin-coated pits (CCPs).
source: The uptake of soluble antigen by the BCR occurs predominantly via clathrin-coated pits (CCPs) (Stoddart et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The uptake of antigens from antigen-presenting immune or stromal cells requires additional forces generated by the acto-myosin cytoskeleton through the formation of B cell immune synapses.
source: In contrast, the uptake of antigens from antigen-presenting immune or stromal cells requires additional forces generated by the acto-myosin cytoskeleton through the formation of B cell immune synapses (Batista et al., 2001; Fleire, 2006; Natkanski et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Myosin IIa is not required for endocytosis of soluble antigens.
source: Myosin IIa is thought to be central to generation of these forces, because it is not required for endocytosis of soluble antigens, but promotes force-mediated antigen extraction from presenting cells in vitro and in vivo (Hoogeboom et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Myosin IIa promotes force-mediated antigen extraction from presenting cells in vitro and in vivo.
source: Myosin IIa is thought to be central to generation of these forces, because it is not required for endocytosis of soluble antigens, but promotes force-mediated antigen extraction from presenting cells in vitro and in vivo (Hoogeboom et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Synaptic actin polymerization is mediated by two mechanisms: the Arp2/3 complex producing branched actin networks, and formins producing linear actin filaments.
source: Synaptic actin polymerization is mediated by two mechanisms: the Arp2/3 complex producing branched actin networks, and formins producing linear actin filaments (Blanchoin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In naive B cells interacting with stiff experimental substrates, F-actin forms a prominent peripheral ring resembling lamellipodia, and an area with contractile arcs, while the synapse center is clear of actin.
source: Indeed, in naive B cells interacting with stiff experimental substrates, such as glass or glass-supported planar lipid bilayers, F-actin forms a prominent peripheral ring resembling lamellipodia, and an area with contractile arcs, while the synapse center is clear of actin (Bolger-Munro et al., 2019; Fleire, 2006; Freeman et al., 2011; Treanor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: B cell synapses contain prominent, but poorly characterized F-actin spots.
source: However, B cell synapses also contain prominent, but poorly characterized F-actin spots (Keppler et al., 2015; Nowosad et al., 2016; Treanor et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Actin foci were observed in T cell synapses on planar lipid bilayers, where they colocalize with T cell receptor microclusters.
source: Similar spots, termed actin foci, were recently observed in T cell synapses on planar lipid bilayers, where they colocalize with T cell receptor microclusters (Kumari et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Antigen uptake from stiff substrates is mechanically inefficient and antigens are instead enzymatically digested out through the release of lytic enzymes into the synaptic cleft.
source: Nevertheless, the relevance of this actin organization for B cell antigen extraction is unclear as antigen uptake from these stiff substrates is mechanically inefficient and antigens are instead enzymatically digested out through the release of lytic enzymes into the synaptic cleft (Spillane and Tolar, 2017; Yuseff et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Studies using soft substrates, such as plasma membrane sheets (PMSs), found that actin formed abundant foci throughout the synapse with little central clearance.
source: In contrast, studies using soft substrates, such as plasma membrane sheets (PMSs), which promote mechanical antigen extraction similar to that occurring with live antigen presenting cells, found that actin formed abundant foci throughout the synapse with little central clearance (Natkanski et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Actin foci were highly dynamic and colocalized with membrane invaginations during antigen uptake.
source: These actin foci were highly dynamic and colocalized with membrane invaginations during antigen uptake, suggesting their involvement in antigen extraction.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work (Natkanski et al., 2013).

claim: Between 5 and 20 min after synapse formation, the Lifeact-labeled F-actin was distributed throughout the synapse in a range of small structures including actin foci and short fibers.
source: Total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy time-lapses showed that after initial cell spreading, between 5 and 20 min after synapse formation, the Lifeact-labeled F-actin was distributed throughout the synapse in a range of small structures including actin foci and short fibers (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: During the first 20 min after synapse formation, B cells were extracting the antigen.
source: 3D imaging verified that during these 20 min, B cells were extracting the antigen as previously described (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by 3D imaging data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The F-actin was highly dynamic and the foci and fibers were appearing stochastically, and often, merged, split or interconverted between each other.
source: TIRF microscopy with a 100 ms time resolution showed that the F-actin was highly dynamic and that the foci and fibers were appearing stochastically, and often, merged, split or interconverted between each other (Video 1, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by high-resolution time-lapse microscopy data shown in Video 1.

claim: Foci numbers per area remained stable at about 5 per 10 μm2 during the 20 min of imaging.
source: Segmentation of actin foci and fibers from time-lapse microscopy of the primary mouse B cells showed that foci numbers per area remained stable at about 5 per 10 μm2 during the 20 min of imaging (Figure 1D,E)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Most individual foci persisted for less than 5 s.
source: Segmentation of actin foci and fibers from time-lapse microscopy of the primary mouse B cells showed that foci numbers per area remained stable at about 5 per 10 μm2 during the 20 min of imaging (Figure 1D,E), but that most individual foci persisted for less than 5 s (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: A similar pattern of foci and interconnecting fibers was observed in the human Ramos cell line.
source: A similar pattern of foci and interconnecting fibers was also observed in the human Ramos cell line, a commonly used B cell lymphoma line, although these cells were larger and had more filopodia emanating from the sides of the synapse (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Ramos cells were larger and had more filopodia emanating from the sides of the synapse compared to primary mouse B cells.
source: A similar pattern of foci and interconnecting fibers was also observed in the human Ramos cell line, a commonly used B cell lymphoma line, although these cells were larger and had more filopodia emanating from the sides of the synapse (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Super-resolution reconstruction of the F-actin showed numerous dense actin foci, interspersed by a sparse network of fibers.
source: Super-resolution reconstruction of the F-actin showed numerous dense actin foci (Figure 1I), interspersed by a sparse network of fibers (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by dSTORM imaging data shown in Figure 1I,J.

claim: The pattern of actin foci and fibers filled the body of the synapse and was surrounded by thin lamellipodia.
source: This pattern filled the body of the synapse and was surrounded by thin lamellipodia (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is supported by dSTORM imaging data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Some actin foci transiently coincide with antigen clusters.
source: Dual color live-cell TIRF microscopy indicated that although the actin structures did not overtly colocalise with antigen, some actin foci did transiently coincide with antigen clusters (Video 2), in line with previous data.
evidence: This is supported by dual-color live-cell microscopy data shown in Video 2.

claim: Antigen clusters that were being internalized were lifted several hundred nanometers from the PMSs.
source: Antigen clusters that were being internalized could be identified, because they were lifted several hundred nanometers from the PMSs.
evidence: This is supported by 3D super-resolution imaging data.

claim: Lifted clusters of antigen were surrounded by dense F-actin foci from the sides.
source: Such lifted clusters of antigen were surrounded by dense F-actin foci from the sides (Figure 1M,N).
evidence: This is supported by 3D super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 1M,N.

claim: More than 20% of actin foci extended more than 200 nm into the cell.
source: Measurement of the height of all the actin foci showed that more than 20% of them extended more than 200 nm into the cell (Figure 1O).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of 3D imaging data shown in Figure 1O.

claim: Foci are the actin structures associated with antigen movement into the cell and likely correspond to actin spots previously associated with membrane invaginations.
source: This suggests that foci are the actin structures associated with antigen movement into the cell and thus likely correspond to actin spots previously associated with membrane invaginations (Natkanski et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the imaging data and comparison to previous work.

claim: The actin foci interact with antigen clusters from the sides or from below.
source: The 3D STORM reconstruction also indicates that the actin foci interact with antigen clusters from the sides or from below, suggesting that they are involved in the transport of the antigen to the interior of the cell.
evidence: This is supported by 3D STORM imaging data.

claim: CK666 treatment resulted in a loss of actin foci, which were instead replaced by abundant actin fibers.
source: Super-resolution imaging showed that CK666 treatment resulted in a loss of actin foci, which were instead replaced by abundant actin fibers (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Treatment with SMIFH2 primarily dispersed the fibers in between foci.
source: In contrast, treatment with SMIFH2 primarily dispersed the fibers in between foci (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Quantification of fast timelapse imaging of CK666-treated B cells confirmed reduction in foci numbers.
source: Quantification of fast timelapse imaging of CK666-treated B cells confirmed reduction in foci numbers (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In CK666-treated B cells, the residual fibers were dynamic, growing, shrinking and curving rapidly.
source: Quantification of fast timelapse imaging of CK666-treated B cells confirmed reduction in foci numbers (Figure 2B) and showed that the residual fibers were dynamic, growing, shrinking and curving rapidly (Video 4).
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Video 4.

claim: In SMIFH2-treated B cells, foci numbers were increased.
source: On the other hand, in SMIFH2-treated B cells, foci numbers were increased, although their lateral movement was arrested and their dynamics stunted (Video 4, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2B and Video 4.

claim: In SMIFH2-treated B cells, foci lateral movement was arrested and their dynamics stunted.
source: On the other hand, in SMIFH2-treated B cells, foci numbers were increased, although their lateral movement was arrested and their dynamics stunted (Video 4, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2B and Video 4.

claim: The actin foci are branched-actin structures generated by the Arp2/3 complex.
source: These results suggested that the actin foci are branched-actin structures generated by the Arp2/3 complex, while the interspersed fibers are linear actin filaments or filament bundles produced by formins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the inhibitor studies.

claim: The interspersed fibers are linear actin filaments or filament bundles produced by formins.
source: These results suggested that the actin foci are branched-actin structures generated by the Arp2/3 complex, while the interspersed fibers are linear actin filaments or filament bundles produced by formins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the inhibitor studies.

claim: All three gRNAs targeting ARPC2 greatly reduced the average levels of the ARPC2 protein in the targeted cell population.
source: All three gRNAs greatly reduced the average levels of the ARPC2 protein in the targeted cell population (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: All three gRNAs targeting ARPC2 reduced the numbers of actin foci and promoted production of actin fibers across the synapse and in filopodia.
source: All three gRNAs reduced the numbers of actin foci and promoted production of actin fibers across the synapse and in filopodia (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and quantitative data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: ARPC2 is essential for production of actin foci in the B cell synapse.
source: Thus, ARPC2 is essential for production of actin foci in the B cell synapse.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CRISPR targeting experiments.

claim: Targeting of DIAPH1 resulted in a subtle decrease in the number of actin foci.
source: Imaging F-actin and quantification of actin foci revealed that targeting of the formins resulted in little change of the synaptic actin pattern (Figure 2F), although quantification showed a subtle decrease in the number of actin foci in cells targeted with the DIAPH1 gRNA, and a small increase in cells targeted with FMNL1 or both DIAPH1 and FMNL1 gRNAs (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Targeting of FMNL1 resulted in a small increase in the number of actin foci.
source: Imaging F-actin and quantification of actin foci revealed that targeting of the formins resulted in little change of the synaptic actin pattern (Figure 2F), although quantification showed a subtle decrease in the number of actin foci in cells targeted with the DIAPH1 gRNA, and a small increase in cells targeted with FMNL1 or both DIAPH1 and FMNL1 gRNAs (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Targeting of both DIAPH1 and FMNL1 resulted in a small increase in the number of actin foci.
source: Imaging F-actin and quantification of actin foci revealed that targeting of the formins resulted in little change of the synaptic actin pattern (Figure 2F), although quantification showed a subtle decrease in the number of actin foci in cells targeted with the DIAPH1 gRNA, and a small increase in cells targeted with FMNL1 or both DIAPH1 and FMNL1 gRNAs (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Neither DIAPH1 nor FMNL1 are required for the formation of actin foci.
source: Therefore, neither DIAPH1 nor FMNL1 are required for the formation of actin foci, and they are redundant in production of the filaments outside of the foci.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CRISPR targeting experiments.

claim: DIAPH1 and FMNL1 are redundant in production of the filaments outside of the foci.
source: Therefore, neither DIAPH1 nor FMNL1 are required for the formation of actin foci, and they are redundant in production of the filaments outside of the foci.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CRISPR targeting experiments.

claim: ARCP2-mRuby localized predominantly in round or slightly elongated spots that corresponded to phalloidin-labeled actin foci.
source: ARCP2-mRuby localized predominantly in round or slightly elongated spots that corresponded to phalloidin-labeled actin foci (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: ARPC2-mRuby closely followed the dynamics of actin in foci visualized in time-lapse imaging.
source: ARPC2-mRuby also closely followed the dynamics of actin in foci visualized in time-lapse imaging of Ramos cells co-expressing Lifeact-GFP (Figure 3B, Video 6).
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Video 6.

claim: The ARPC2-mRuby-positive actin foci were surrounded by short, ARPC2-mRuby-negative actin fibers.
source: The ARPC2-mRuby-positive actin foci were surrounded by short, ARPC2-mRuby-negative actin fibers, which were frequently seen dynamically emanating from the foci and sometimes transiently connecting to other foci (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Short actin fibers were frequently seen dynamically emanating from the foci and sometimes transiently connecting to other foci.
source: The ARPC2-mRuby-positive actin foci were surrounded by short, ARPC2-mRuby-negative actin fibers, which were frequently seen dynamically emanating from the foci and sometimes transiently connecting to other foci (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the cell periphery the fibers grew into filopodia, while in the center of the synapse, the short fibers did not correspond to membrane structures.
source: Simultaneous labeling of the Ramos B cell plasma membrane using the lipid dye DiD indicated that while in the cell periphery the fibers grew into filopodia, in the center of the synapse, the short fibers did not correspond to membrane structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: DIAPH1-mRuby localization was more diffuse than that of ARPC2, but some DIAPH1-mRuby spots were visible and they often overlapped with actin foci.
source: DIAPH1-mRuby localization was more diffuse than that of ARPC2, but some DIAPH1-mRuby spots were also visible and they often overlapped with actin foci (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: DIAPH1 spots followed the dynamics of actin foci less precisely than ARPC2 spots did.
source: However, live cell imaging indicated that DIAPH1 spots followed the dynamics of actin foci less precisely than ARPC2 spots did (Figure 3E, Video 7).
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 3E and Video 7.

claim: Spots of DIAPH1-mRuby were seen producing actin fibers growing out of them, including filopodia.
source: The spots of DIAPH1-mRuby were also seen producing actin fibers growing out of them, including filopodia (Figure 3F, Video 7).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3F and Video 7.

claim: ARPC2-mRuby was significantly enriched in actin foci, while it was depleted in fibers.
source: Quantification confirmed that ARPC2-mRuby was significantly enriched in actin foci, while it was depleted in fibers (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: A significant fraction of actin foci directly colocalized with ARPC2 spots and vice versa.
source: In addition, dual segmentation of the ARPC2 spots and actin foci showed that a significant fraction of actin foci directly colocalized with ARPC2 spots and vice versa (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3H.

claim: DIAPH1-mRuby was enriched in actin foci as compared to fibers.
source: DIAPH1-mRuby was also enriched in actin foci as compared to fibers (Figure 3G)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: DIAPH1-mRuby spots significantly colocalized with actin foci.
source: DIAPH1-mRuby was also enriched in actin foci as compared to fibers (Figure 3G) and DIAPH1-mRuby spots significantly colocalized with actin foci (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3I.

claim: DIAPH1-mRuby enrichment in foci and rates of colocalization were significantly lower than that of ARPC2.
source: However, its enrichment in foci and rates of colocalization were significantly lower than that of ARPC2.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3G,H,I.

claim: Actin foci contain predominantly branched actin marked with ARPC2, and they represent the dominant branched-actin structures of the B cell synapse.
source: Thus, actin foci contain predominantly branched actin marked with ARPC2, and they represent the dominant branched-actin structures of the B cell synapse.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the localization and colocalization data.

claim: The foci associate with DIAPH1, which does not contribute to foci generation, but produces short linear filaments that surround and interconnect them.
source: Nevertheless, the foci also associate with DIAPH1, which does not contribute to foci generation, but produces short linear filaments that surround and interconnect them.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the localization data and CRISPR experiments.

claim: Most of the active myosin IIa did not overlap with the most prominent F-actin structures, although it was localized in close proximity to both actin foci and actin fibers.
source: This imaging showed that most of the active myosin IIa did not overlap with the most prominent F-actin structures, although it was localized in close proximity to both actin foci and actin fibers (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: The inhibition of the ATPase activity of myosin IIa with para-nitroblebbistatin only modestly reduced foci numbers.
source: In addition, the inhibition of the ATPase activity of myosin IIa with para-nitroblebbistatin only modestly reduced foci numbers (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D, Video 8), despite strongly impairing antigen extraction (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D and Video 8.

claim: Para-nitroblebbistatin strongly impaired antigen extraction.
source: In addition, the inhibition of the ATPase activity of myosin IIa with para-nitroblebbistatin only modestly reduced foci numbers (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D, Video 8), despite strongly impairing antigen extraction (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Actin foci are not myosin IIa-dependent contractile structures, although they are subtly regulated by its motor activity.
source: Thus, actin foci are not myosin IIa-dependent contractile structures, although they are subtly regulated by its motor activity, which is consistent with their branched actin structure and a rapid turnover.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the myosin IIa inhibition experiments.

claim: Total phosphotyrosine and phospho-CD19 signals had significantly higher enrichment in actin foci than in actin fibers.
source: All phosphotyrosine signals had low colocalization with actin, however, we detected significantly higher enrichment of total phosphotyrosine and phospho-CD19 signals in actin foci than in actin fibers (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Phosphorylated BLNK was only weakly enriched in foci, but was still highly excluded from fibers.
source: Phosphorylated BLNK was only weakly enriched in foci, but was still highly excluded from fibers (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Actin foci are the predominant actin structure associated with BCR signaling.
source: Thus, actin foci are the predominant actin structure associated with BCR signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the phosphotyrosine localization data.

claim: The actin architecture composed of foci and interspersed fibers did not require antigen-induced stimulation of the BCR.
source: However, we observed that the actin architecture composed of foci and interspersed fibers did not require antigen-induced stimulation of the BCR, as it was similar in B cells interacting with PMSs loaded with non-stimulatory anti-MHC I or anti-MHC II antibodies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Video 9), with numbers of foci even slightly increased (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B and Video 9.

claim: Numbers of foci were slightly increased in B cells interacting with PMSs loaded with non-stimulatory anti-MHC I or anti-MHC II antibodies.
source: However, we observed that the actin architecture composed of foci and interspersed fibers did not require antigen-induced stimulation of the BCR, as it was similar in B cells interacting with PMSs loaded with non-stimulatory anti-MHC I or anti-MHC II antibodies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Video 9), with numbers of foci even slightly increased (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The actin foci were accentuated by treatment of antigen-activated B cells with the Src-family inhibitor PP2, despite the reduction in total F-actin.
source: The actin foci, were also accentuated by treatment of antigen-activated B cells with the Src-family inhibitor PP2, despite the reduction in total F-actin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D, Video 10).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and quantitative data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D and Video 10.

claim: Inhibition of Syk using the inhibitor P505-15 led to a more modest increase in foci numbers.
source: Inhibition of Syk using the inhibitor P505-15 led to a more modest increase in foci numbers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D, Video 10).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D and Video 10.

claim: The foci in both PP2 and P505-15 treated B cells had increased lifetimes and reduced lateral mobilities.
source: However, the foci in both PP2 and P505-15 treated B cells had increased lifetimes and reduced lateral mobilities (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: While antigen stimulation is not required for foci formation, BCR signaling regulates synaptic actin architecture including foci dynamics.
source: Thus, while antigen stimulation is not required for foci formation, BCR signaling regulates synaptic actin architecture including foci dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the inhibitor studies.

claim: ARPC2 clusters colocalized with antigen clusters at the time of extraction and endocytosis.
source: We observed that ARPC2 clusters, colocalized with antigen clusters at the time of extraction and endocytosis (Video 11), while DIAPH1 did not (Video 12).
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Video 11.

claim: DIAPH1 did not colocalize with antigen clusters at the time of extraction and endocytosis.
source: We observed that ARPC2 clusters, colocalized with antigen clusters at the time of extraction and endocytosis (Video 11), while DIAPH1 did not (Video 12).
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Video 12.

claim: CLTA-mCherry signal was significantly enriched in actin foci as compared to actin fibers.
source: Quantification showed that CLTA-mCherry signal was significantly enriched in actin foci as compared to actin fibers (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: About 3% of foci directly colocalized with CCPs, and 7% of CCPs colocalized with actin foci, rates that were significantly above those expected from random co-localization.
source: Although only about 3% of foci directly colocalized with CCPs, and 7% of CCPs colocalized with actin foci, these rates were significantly above those expected from random co-localization of these structures (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: While most actin foci are independent of CCPs, a small number of them coincides with a fraction of CCPs at any given time.
source: Thus, while most actin foci are independent of CCPs, a small number of them coincides with a fraction of CCPs at any given time, consistent with the transient nature of actin polymerization during clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the colocalization data.

claim: Internalization of soluble surrogate antigen anti-Igκ F(ab')2 by naive mouse B cells was only very modestly sensitive to inhibition of either of the Arp2/3 complex or formins, or to complete block in actin polymerization by cytochalasin D.
source: We found that internalization of soluble surrogate antigen anti-Igκ F(ab')2 or soluble transferrin by naive mouse B cells was only very modestly sensitive to inhibition of either of the Arp2/3 complex or formins, or to complete block in actin polymerization by cytochalasin D (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Internalization of soluble transferrin by naive mouse B cells was only very modestly sensitive to inhibition of either of the Arp2/3 complex or formins, or to complete block in actin polymerization by cytochalasin D.
source: We found that internalization of soluble surrogate antigen anti-Igκ F(ab')2 or soluble transferrin by naive mouse B cells was only very modestly sensitive to inhibition of either of the Arp2/3 complex or formins, or to complete block in actin polymerization by cytochalasin D (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Internalization of soluble anti-IgM F(ab')2 antibodies by Ramos cells was not significantly inhibited by blocking Arp2/3 or formin activity.
source: Similarly, internalization of soluble anti-IgM F(ab')2 antibodies by Ramos cells was not significantly inhibited by blocking Arp2/3 or formin activity, although some inhibition was achieved by treatment with cytochalasin D (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Some inhibition of internalization of soluble anti-IgM F(ab')2 antibodies by Ramos cells was achieved by treatment with cytochalasin D.
source: Similarly, internalization of soluble anti-IgM F(ab')2 antibodies by Ramos cells was not significantly inhibited by blocking Arp2/3 or formin activity, although some inhibition was achieved by treatment with cytochalasin D (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The uptake of soluble antigen is relatively independent of actin polymerization.
source: Thus, the uptake of soluble antigen is relatively independent of actin polymerization.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the soluble antigen internalization experiments.

claim: Extraction of the surrogate antigens by either primary cells or Ramos cells from PMSs was completely abolished by blocking actin polymerization with latrunculin A.
source: In contrast, extraction of the surrogate antigens by either primary cells or Ramos cells from PMSs was completely abolished by blocking actin polymerization with latrunculin A, indicating importance of actin polymerization for force-mediated uptake of membrane antigens (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Actin polymerization is important for force-mediated uptake of membrane antigens.
source: In contrast, extraction of the surrogate antigens by either primary cells or Ramos cells from PMSs was completely abolished by blocking actin polymerization with latrunculin A, indicating importance of actin polymerization for force-mediated uptake of membrane antigens (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the latrunculin A experiments.

claim: The uptake of antigens from PMSs was markedly sensitive to inhibition of Arp2/3 by CK666.
source: The uptake of antigens from PMSs was also markedly sensitive to inhibition of Arp2/3 by CK666 (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: CRISPR-mediated targeting of ARPC2 in Ramos cells decreased antigen uptake from PMSs.
source: In addition, CRISPR-mediated targeting of ARPC2 in Ramos cells decreased antigen uptake from PMSs (Figure 5E), significantly for two of the three gRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Arp2/3 activity is critical for uptake of antigens from PMSs.
source: Thus, Arp2/3 activity is critical for uptake of antigens from PMSs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CK666 and CRISPR experiments.

claim: Inhibition of formins by SMIFH2 strongly reduced synaptic antigen internalization in both primary B cells and Ramos cells.
source: However, inhibition of formins by SMIFH2 strongly reduced synaptic antigen internalization in both primary B cells and Ramos cells (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Both Arp2/3 and formins are important for the uptake of antigens from the synapse.
source: Thus, these results overall support the conclusion that both Arp2/3 and formins are important for the uptake of antigens from the synapse, indicating the importance of both the formation and the dynamics of the actin foci and further support from actin fibers in extraction of membrane-presented antigens.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the inhibitor and CRISPR experiments.

claim: Approximately 40% of PMS deformation pulling events could be assigned to actin foci or fibers.
source: Approximately 40% of these pulling events could be assigned to actin foci or fibers using this analysis (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: About 30% of pulling events occurred with actin fibers, while less than 10% associated with foci.
source: About 30% occurred with actin fibers, while less than 10% associated with foci (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The actin foci were three times more efficient at applying forces on the PMSs than fibers.
source: However, correcting for the much smaller area of the cells occupied by foci showed that the actin foci were three times more efficient at applying forces on the PMSs than fibers (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Both foci and fibers apply pulling forces on the antigen-presenting membrane, but with different geometry and efficiency.
source: Thus, both foci and fibers apply pulling forces on the antigen-presenting membrane, but with different geometry and efficiency.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the PMS deformation analysis.

claim: The overall number of membrane pulling events was not affected by either CK666 or SMIFH2 compared to the DMSO control.
source: We found that the overall number of membrane pulling events was not affected by either of the inhibitors compared to the DMSO control (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Ramos cells treated with CK666 often generated elongated membrane structures in the synapse, with some cells producing excessively long and convoluted membrane tubules and ridges.
source: However, Ramos cells treated with CK666 often generated elongated membrane structures in the synapse, with some cells producing excessively long and convoluted membrane tubules and ridges (Figure 6G, Figure 6—video 2–4).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6G and Figure 6—video 2–4.

claim: The pulling activity of CK666-treated Ramos cells resulted in fewer synapses containing only spots and more synapses dominated by tubules.
source: The analysis showed that the pulling activity of CK666-treated Ramos cells resulted in fewer synapses containing only spots and more synapses dominated by tubules (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Formin-generated fibers predominantly contribute to long-range antigen movement along the plasma membrane.
source: These data are consistent with formin-generated fibers predominantly contributing to long-range antigen movement along the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on the CK666 treatment results.

claim: Coordinated function of both Arp2/3 and formins is required to extract antigen in a manner that leads to efficient endocytosis.
source: Overall, while actin polymerization either through Arp2/3 or formins exerts mechanical forces in the immune synapse, coordinated function of both of these actin polymerization mechanisms is required to extract antigen in a manner that leads to efficient endocytosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mechanical activity analysis.

claim: After initial cell spreading, the B cell synapse contains a stochastic pattern of foci and fibers.
source: Our data show that after initial cell spreading, the B cell synapse contains a stochastic pattern of foci and fibers.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Foci and fibers are generated locally in the synapse by transient activities of the Arp2/3 complex and formins, respectively.
source: These structures are generated locally in the synapse by transient activities of the Arp2/3 complex and formins, respectively and are important for antigen extraction.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Foci and fibers are important for antigen extraction.
source: These structures are generated locally in the synapse by transient activities of the Arp2/3 complex and formins, respectively and are important for antigen extraction.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The foci and fibers are often generated from each other during their constant turnover.
source: Despite their different mechanism of production, the foci and fibers are closely related as they are often generated from each other during their constant turnover.
evidence: This is based on the observation of foci and fiber dynamics.

claim: Colocalization of both Arp2/3 and formins with the actin foci leads to production of both branched actin and linear filaments from the same sites.
source: This is also illustrated by colocalization of both Arp2/3 and formins with the actin foci, leading to production of both branched actin and linear filaments from the same sites.
evidence: This is based on the localization data.

claim: This actin behavior produces network-like connectivity that is distinct from the actin structure of CD4 and CD8 T cell synapses.
source: This actin behavior produces network-like connectivity that is distinct from the actin structure of CD4 (Kumari et al., 2015; Murugesan et al., 2016) and CD8 (Ritter et al., 2015) T cell synapses and also differs from B cell synapses formed with stiff substrates, where peripheral lamellipodial actin, and acto-myosin contractile rings occupy distinct domains of the synapse (Bolger-Munro et al., 2019; Fleire, 2006).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work supported by citations.

claim: The actin behavior in B cell synapses differs from B cell synapses formed with stiff substrates, where peripheral lamellipodial actin, and acto-myosin contractile rings occupy distinct domains of the synapse.
source: This actin behavior produces network-like connectivity that is distinct from the actin structure of CD4 (Kumari et al., 2015; Murugesan et al., 2016) and CD8 (Ritter et al., 2015) T cell synapses and also differs from B cell synapses formed with stiff substrates, where peripheral lamellipodial actin, and acto-myosin contractile rings occupy distinct domains of the synapse (Bolger-Munro et al., 2019; Fleire, 2006).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work supported by citations.

claim: When B cells extract antigens from live antigen-presenting cells, actin foci and fibers form nodes and edges in a loosely connected network, whose function is required for efficient antigen extraction.
source: We speculate that when B cells extract antigens from live antigen-presenting cells, actin foci and fibers form nodes and edges in a loosely connected network, whose function is required for efficient antigen extraction.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Stochastic Arp2/3 activation produces actin foci by local bursts of branching of preexisting short filaments.
source: In this model, stochastic Arp2/3 activation produces actin foci by local bursts of branching of preexisting short filaments.
evidence: This is part of a speculative model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Branched actin polymerization may either push on the membrane to generate protrusions, or synergize with BCR-dependent signaling and endocytic proteins to produce an invagination of the plasma membrane and extract the antigen.
source: Branched actin polymerization may either push on the membrane to generate protrusions, similarly as it happens in podosomes (van den Dries et al., 2019), or synergize with BCR-dependent signaling and endocytic proteins to produce an invagination of the plasma membrane and extract the antigen.
evidence: This is a speculative model with a citation to support the podosome comparison.

claim: Formin-generated filaments may stabilize the foci by surrounding and connecting them, which could help to direct the foci-generated forces perpendicularly to the plasma membrane.
source: Formin-generated filaments may stabilize the foci by surrounding and connecting them, which, along with crosslinking and tensioning by myosin IIa, could help to direct the foci-generated forces perpendicularly to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the experimental findings.

claim: The linear filament polymerization out of the foci may help to extend the range of the inward movement or enhance the extraction force directly.
source: In addition, the linear filament polymerization out of the foci may help to extend the range of the inward movement or enhance the extraction force directly.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the experimental findings.

claim: The importance of the Arp2/3 complex in foci formation is consistent with previous data linking activators of the Arp2/3 complex, WAS WIPF1 and ITSN2, with foci formation in T cells and in B cells.
source: The importance of the Arp2/3 complex in foci formation is consistent with previous data linking activators of the Arp2/3 complex, WAS WIPF1 and ITSN2, with foci formation in T cells (Janssen et al., 2016; Kumari et al., 2015) and in B cells (Burbage et al., 2018; Keppler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work supported by citations.

claim: Both Arp2/3 and formins are active throughout the B cell synapse during antigen uptake without large-scale segregation.
source: Thus, both Arp2/3 and formins are active throughout the B cell synapse during antigen uptake without large-scale segregation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the localization data.

claim: The data extend previous knowledge of the importance of Arp2/3 complex in the generation of the lamellipodial actin ring and centripetal membrane flow important for B cell adhesion, BCR signaling and B cell activation.
source: Our data thus extend previous knowledge of the importance of Arp2/3 complex in the generation of the lamellipodial actin ring and centripetal membrane flow important for B cell adhesion, BCR signaling and B cell activation (Bolger-Munro et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work supported by a citation.

claim: Arp2/3-generated actin foci are intimately associated with antigen extraction.
source: Our data also show that Arp2/3-generated actin foci are intimately associated with antigen extraction, as seen in instances of their presence at the sites of antigen endocytosis and their close, albeit stochastic, relationship to BCR tyrosine-phosphorylated proteins and CCPs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the colocalization data.

claim: Forces that lead to antigen extraction are dependent on new actin polymerization in actin foci.
source: Our model thus suggests that forces that lead to antigen extraction are dependent on new actin polymerization in actin foci.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the experimental findings.

claim: F-actin is continuously accumulating on individual membrane invaginations during B cell antigen uptake.
source: This hypothesis is supported by previous observation that F-actin is continuously accumulating on individual membrane invaginations during B cell antigen uptake (Natkanski et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: 3D superresolution imaging shows that actin is associated with the sides of the antigen clusters during internalization, where polymerization could contribute to membrane invagination.
source: In addition, our 3D superresolution imaging shows that actin is associated with the sides of the antigen clusters during internalization, where polymerization could contribute to membrane invagination.
evidence: This is based on the 3D STORM imaging data.

claim: Foci-like structures were associated with antigen extraction from gel-like substrates, where they were found protruding into the substrate.
source: Foci-like structures were also associated with antigen extraction from gel-like substrates in a recent study, where they were found protruding into the substrate (Kumari et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: It is possible that Arp2/3 generated actin structures can both push and pull on the antigen presenting cell, eventually using actin polymerization for antigen extraction.
source: It is thus possible that Arp2/3 generated actin structures can both push and pull on the antigen presenting cell, eventually using actin polymerization for antigen extraction.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the data.

claim: The branched actin polymerization in the foci is not sufficient to extract antigen as inhibitions of formin and myosin IIa activities also inhibit antigen uptake.
source: Nevertheless, our data also indicate that the branched actin polymerization in the foci is not sufficient to extract antigen as inhibitions of formin and myosin IIa activities also inhibit antigen uptake.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the inhibitor studies.

claim: Formins together with myosin IIa provide stability to actin polymerization in the foci that helps the branched actin to expand in between the future base and tip of the invagination, generating an inward force.
source: Since formin inhibition altered foci dynamics, we hypothesize that formins together with myosin IIa provide stability to actin polymerization in the foci that helps the branched actin to expand in between the future base and tip of the invagination, generating an inward force, as opposed to a lateral force and a comet-like movement along the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: A similar stabilizing role for myosin contractility was suggested for function of CCPs in other cells types.
source: A similar stabilizing role for myosin contractility was suggested for function of CCPs in other cells types (Chandrasekar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Myosin contractility or fiber dynamics may help to dislodge the antigen from the presenting membrane before endocytosis through actin foci.
source: Alternatively, myosin contractility or fiber dynamics may help to dislodge the antigen from the presenting membrane before endocytosis through actin foci.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative hypothesis.

claim: Formin-mediated actin polymerization out of the foci may extend the range of movement of the foci during late stages of antigen endocytosis.
source: Finally, it is possible that formin-mediated actin polymerization out of the foci extends the range of movement of the foci during late stages of antigen endocytosis.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis.

claim: The latter two points are supported by the observations of cells after pharmacological inhibition of the Arp2/3 complex, when the residual fibers are able to transport antigen clusters and pull large membrane ridges or tubules from the presenting membrane both by their contractile motion and by their growth.
source: The latter two points are supported by the observations of cells after pharmacological inhibition of the Arp2/3 complex, when the residual fibers are able to transport antigen clusters and pull large membrane ridges or tubules from the presenting membrane both by their contractile motion and by their growth.
evidence: This is based on the CK666 treatment observations.

claim: The actin organization and mechanism of antigen extraction studied here pertains primarily to the synapses formed by naive and memory B cells, where antigen extraction is directly followed by endocytosis.
source: The actin organization and mechanism of antigen extraction studied here pertains primarily to the synapses formed by naive and memory B cells, where antigen extraction is directly followed by endocytosis (Nowosad et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a clarification of the scope of the study with a citation.

claim: In germinal center B cells, peripheral actomyosin-rich pod like protrusions extract antigen and transport it by outward actin flow along the plasma membrane away from the antigen-presenting surface.
source: In these cells, peripheral actomyosin-rich pod like protrusions extract antigen and transport it by outward actin flow along the plasma membrane away from the antigen-presenting surface (Kwak et al., 2018; Nowosad et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Arp2/3-dependent actin polymerization is likely a general requirement for antigen extraction from antigen-presenting cells.
source: Arp2/3-dependent actin polymerization is therefore likely a general requirement for antigen extraction from antigen-presenting cells.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the data and comparison to germinal center B cells.

claim: The formation of the actin foci in naive B cells does not require antigen stimulation.
source: Unexpectedly, our data show that the formation of the actin foci in naive B cells does not require antigen stimulation.
evidence: This is based on the experiments with non-stimulatory antibodies.

claim: The actin foci may be generated continuously as a general property of the B cell cortical cytoskeleton.
source: The actin foci may thus be generated continuously as a general property of the B cell cortical cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observation that foci form without antigen stimulation.

claim: The majority of actin foci in the synapse do not associate with antigen clusters, or with CCPs.
source: In agreement with this observation, the majority of actin foci in the synapse do not associate with antigen clusters, or with CCPs.
evidence: This is based on the colocalization data.

claim: A small fraction of actin foci did associate with antigen clusters and to a lower degree with CCPs.
source: However, a small fraction of actin foci did associate with antigen clusters and to a lower degree with CCPs.
evidence: This is based on the colocalization data.

claim: A local synergy between BCR signaling, actin dynamics and CCP formation at BCR clusters either enhances the rates of formation of endocytic structures, or stabilizes otherwise abortive events to promote efficient antigen uptake.
source: Since BCR signaling regulates actin dynamics (Tolar, 2017), including foci dynamics shown here, as well as CCP dynamics (Natkanski et al., 2013; Stoddart et al., 2002) we speculate that a local synergy between BCR signaling, actin dynamics and CCP formation at BCR clusters either enhances the rates of formation of endocytic structures, or stabilizes otherwise abortive events to promote efficient antigen uptake.
evidence: This is a speculative model with citations to support the role of BCR signaling.

claim: The organization of the BCR, and other signaling receptors on B cell surfaces critically depend on actin structure.
source: The organization of the BCR, and other signaling receptors on B cell surfaces critically depend on actin structure (Mattila et al., 2016) and defects in actin polymerization contribute to the dysregulation of signaling in primary immunodeficiencies and in autoimmunity (Tolar, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Defects in actin polymerization contribute to the dysregulation of signaling in primary immunodeficiencies and in autoimmunity.
source: The organization of the BCR, and other signaling receptors on B cell surfaces critically depend on actin structure (Mattila et al., 2016) and defects in actin polymerization contribute to the dysregulation of signaling in primary immunodeficiencies and in autoimmunity (Tolar, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.
